resources.string: The Aive crashed or stopped responding earlier, and a report (stack trace, app version, Android version, device model) was sent automatically to the HereLiesAz/aive GitHub issue tracker. You can turn automatic crash reports off any time in Settings → Crash Reports.

This copy was installed outside Google Play, so the update comes from GitHub. Open the release page, download the APK, then tap it to install; Android may ask you to allow installs from your browser. Installing over this copy keeps your projects, settings, credentials, roles, and workflows.
An update for The Aive is available
An update is available through Google Play.
Google Play builds connect to Gemini through the official API. The installed-app bridge is available in GitHub releases.
The Gemini app was not detected. You can still connect Gemini with an API key.
The installed Gemini app is ready. The Aive can open it in a bounded window and use it as the Gemini transport.
The Gemini app is installed. Enable The Aive · Gemini bridge in Android Accessibility settings to use the signed-in app without an API key.
No Gemini app? Use an API key instead: you can create one for free at Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com).
The Gemini bridge is still off. Open Accessibility settings and turn on The Aive · Gemini bridge, or use an API key.
Notifications are blocked, so you will not see the Remote access status. You can allow them in Android Settings → Apps → The Aive → Notifications.
The Aive could not check for updates. Try again later.
Key rejected. Check the relay address and reconnect.
The relay is rate limiting you. Wait a minute and try again.
Can\'t reach the relay. Check your internet connection and try again.
The relay took too long to answer. Try again.
Remote access could not be changed. Try again, or check the relay address under Advanced.
